core_obligations: Use the quotient-by-coproduct lemma to exhibit every sheaf of sets F as the target of a surjection from a coproduct of representable sheaves h_U^# with U in the basis (proof lines 5471-5476).
Apply the same to the fibre product F_0 x_F F_0 to express F as a coequalizer of a pair of maps between coproducts over index sets I and J with V_j and U_i in the basis (proof lines 5477-5486).

For every finite subset of J find a finite subset of I into which the two maps carry the corresponding coproduct, using quasi-compactness, and conclude that F is a filtered colimit of the finitely presented coequalizers displayed in the statement (proof lines 5487-5515).
Deduce statement (2) for modules over a sheaf of rings by the analogous cokernel presentation, using the direct images j_{U!}O_U in place of the representable sheaves.
proof_roadmap: Present a sheaf as a coequalizer of coproducts of representables.
Cut the index sets to finite subsets using quasi-compactness.
Conclude the filtered colimit presentation and repeat the argument for modules.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that every sheaf of sets (and, for a sheaf of rings, every module) is a filtered colimit of the standard coequalizer (respectively cokernel) presentations whose terms are coproducts of representable sheaves or of the sheaf-theoretic direct images j_{U!}O_U along members of a basis. The proof of the set-theoretic statement uses a surjection onto the sheaf from a coproduct of representables, applies it to the fibre product to exhibit the sheaf as a coequalizer, and then cuts the index sets down to finite subsets using quasi-compactness, so that the sheaf is a filtered colimit of finitely presented pieces (proof lines 5471-5515). H3: the reduction to a coequalizer and the finite-cut argument with quasi-compactness are independent research-level work, not a citation.
